questions.q:
Under PRAHAAR, the national counter-terrorism policy and strategy of the Ministry of Home Affairs, consider the following statements:
1. The local police are the first responder to a terror incident.
2. The National Security Guard functions under the Ministry of Defence as the nodal force for major attacks.
3. The Joint Task Force on Intelligence and the Multi Agency Centre are placed in the Intelligence Bureau.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Local police act first, backed by State and Central anti-terror forces, while the two intelligence platforms sit in the Intelligence Bureau for real-time sharing. Statement 2 is wrong: the NSG works under the Ministry of Home Affairs, although it was created for counter-terror operations and draws many personnel from the Army. It is the nodal national force.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80

questions.q: BOLD-QIT, cited as a pilot under border technology, is best understood as:
o: a satellite constellation used by the Navy to watch deep-sea approaches
a biometric database for travellers at integrated check posts
a tunnel-boring system used to build all-weather Himalayan roads
an electronic surveillance and quick-response system for riverine border stretches where fencing is impractical
questions.e: BOLD-QIT stands for Border Electronically Dominated QRT Interception Technique. It was piloted on the Brahmaputra stretch in Dhubri, Assam, where shifting river channels defeat conventional fencing, and uses sensors and data links so that quick-reaction teams can intercept intruders. It is a component in the wider Comprehensive Integrated Border Management System, whose further stages extend to about 1,955 km of vulnerable border.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71; Dhubri pilot is static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of a pillar of PRAHAAR and a feature associated with it:
1. Prevention : Reintegrating affected communities through doctors, psychologists and lawyers
2. Aggregating capacities : Specialised tactical training by BPR&D and the NSG
3. Aligning international efforts : Mutual Legal Assistance Treaties and extradition arrangements
4. Attenuating conducive conditions : Graded police response for radicalised youth
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2, 3 and 4 are right. Pair 1 is wrong, as reintegration through professionals and community leaders belongs to Recovery and Resilience, the whole-of-society pillar. Prevention instead means intelligence-guided action and protection of critical sectors. The seven-letter structure also has Response and Human Rights. Candidates often confuse the two pillars that address radicalisation and community work, so keep them distinct.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80

questions.q:
PRAHAAR's rule-of-law pillar refers to several laws. Consider the following statements:
1. The 2019 amendment of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 allows individuals to be designated as terrorists.
2. The National Investigation Agency needs prior consent of the State Government before investigating a scheduled offence in that State.
3. The Prevention of Money Laundering Act and the Arms Act were both enacted after the 2008 Mumbai attacks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; earlier only organisations could be so listed. Statement 2 is wrong, as the 2008 NIA Act gives concurrent jurisdiction nationwide without needing State consent, unlike the CBI's position under its own law. Statement 3 is wrong: the Arms Act dates to 1959 and PMLA to 2002. The NIA, however, was indeed set up in response to the 2008 attacks.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80; NIA Act consent position is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The recent profitability of many Indian power distribution companies is viewed as fragile.
Statement-II: Profits in several States arise after large tariff subsidies and takeover of losses by State Governments.
Statement-III: Non-cost-reflective tariffs and unmetered farm supply continue to burden the sector.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both reasons are correct and each explains why the turnaround may not last. Tamil Nadu's reported profit, for example, appeared only after huge subsidy and loss takeover by the State, without which it would show a substantial loss. Tariffs that lag costs and unmetered farm supply leave the underlying gap unresolved. Commentators thus describe the improvement as subsidy-driven rather than efficiency-driven, with future pay revisions adding pressure.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 75-78

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about two indicators of stress in electricity distribution:
1. Aggregate Technical and Commercial loss captures poor billing and poor collection as well as technical line loss.
2. A positive ACS-ARR gap means that the utility recovers less per unit than it costs to supply.
3. Tariffs for consumers are fixed by State Electricity Regulatory Commissions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. The AT&C measure is wider than transmission and distribution loss since it also includes theft, billing inefficiency and unpaid bills. The gap compares Average Cost of Supply with Average Revenue Realised, so a wider gap means selling below cost. Regulators in each State decide tariffs, so timely, independent revisions are central to closing this gap and repairing finances.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 75-78

questions.q: INS Anjadip takes its name from an island located off:
o: Kakinada on the Andhra Pradesh coast
Port Blair in the Andaman Islands
questions.e: Anjadip Island lies off Karwar in Karnataka, near the Navy's major western base. The vessel is the third of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft from GRSE, Kolkata, designed for littoral operations and called a 'Dolphin Hunter', and it carries a hull-mounted sonar named Abhay. Other sites here are plausible because they are also naval or maritime locations, but they are unconnected.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 72

questions.q:
Match the following exercises with the partner country of India:
List-I
A. Harimau Shakti
B. LAMITYE
C. VARUNA
D. FRINJEX
List-II
1. Seychelles
2. France (Navy)
3. France (Army)
4. Malaysia (Army)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Harimau Shakti is with Malaysia, its name drawing on the Malay word for tiger. LAMITYE, Creole for friendship, is with Seychelles. VARUNA is the bilateral naval exercise with France, and FRINJEX is the army exercise with the same country, so remember that one partner can have several exercises. La Perouse and ORION are also multilateral or air engagements involving France.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 23, 27, 28, 71; meaning of names is static

questions.q:
PRAHAAR faces federal coordination challenges. With reference to this, consider the following statements:
1. 'Police' and 'public order' are entries in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. Under Article 355, it is a duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong because these are State List subjects, which is why a uniform template needs State buy-in and why capacity building of State anti-terror squads features among suggested reforms. Article 355 places a protective duty on the Union, but day-to-day policing still rests on States, creating the coordination gap that the new doctrine must work around.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80; Seventh Schedule and Article 355 are static

questions.q:
Which of the following tools or platforms are correctly described in the context of India's border and internal security?
1. NATGRID : Links databases of different agencies for real-time checks
2. Cartosat-2C and RISAT-2A : Unmanned underwater vehicles used against sub-sea intrusion
3. RFID and biometrics : Fast verification of travellers
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Items 1 and 3 are right. NATGRID was conceived after 26/11 so that agencies could cross-check data, and RFID with biometrics supports identity and access control at crossings. Item 2 is wrong: Cartosat-2C and RISAT-2A are Indian satellites used under the space-based surveillance programme to map vulnerable outposts. The underwater domain remains a separate concern, highlighted by attackers' use of the sea on 26/11.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Creation of the Combating Financing of Terrorism Cell in the Ministry of Home Affairs
2. Enactment of the Protection of Human Rights Act
3. Setting up of the National Investigation Agency
4. Enactment of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act
Select the correct order using the code given below.
questions.e: The order is 1967, 1993, 2008 and 2011. The Unlawful Activities law came first and was later strengthened for terrorism. The human rights law followed, and it is now cited in the rule-of-law pillar of PRAHAAR. The NIA arose after the Mumbai attacks of 2008, and the finance cell came in 2011 to target hawala and narcotics money, reflecting a growing focus on funding.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80

questions.q: Feeder segregation, recommended for distribution reform, primarily means:
o: separating generation and transmission companies from one another
separating agricultural and non-agricultural supply lines so farm use can be measured and managed
separating Central and State shares in a tariff order
separating renewable from thermal generation at the regional load despatch centre
questions.e: It separates farm and other feeders in rural networks, giving better measurement of farm consumption, load management and less cross-subsidy. Gujarat, Rajasthan and Karnataka are cited as examples. The other choices describe different concepts: unbundling power utilities, sharing of duties, and despatch of generation. Solar pumps, which NITI Aayog recommended in 2021, are a complementary way of lowering farm supply costs.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 75-78

questions.q:
With reference to the evolution of India's electricity distribution sector, consider the following statements:
1. State Electricity Boards under the Electricity (Supply) Act, 1948 stayed loss-making despite a statutory requirement of a minimum surplus.
2. The Electricity Act, 2003 merged all generation and distribution into a single national board.
3. The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme gives assistance unconditionally to States, irrespective of reform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; Section 59 mandated a 3 per cent return, yet boards made losses. Statement 2 is wrong as the 2003 Act moved the other way, towards unbundling boards and creating competition, with regulators. Statement 3 is wrong because the RDSS ties financial aid to reform milestones, including smart metering, loss reduction and feeder segregation, to improve efficiency and supply reliability.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 75-78; Electricity Act 2003 is static

questions.q:
With reference to the Union Home Minister's call for advanced technology at the borders, consider the following statements:
1. Surges in drone incursions dropping narcotics and weapons are especially reported on the western sector.
2. The proposal for a Border Security Technology Oversight Authority aims at auditing surveillance for legality and misuse.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct. Foreign-based groups use drones to target Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir with arms and drugs, bypassing fences and border outposts. The oversight idea recognises that more sensors and identity checks raise questions of legality and privacy. Alongside these, the BSF plans a unified AI-based smart border observation system. Global models include Israel's Smart Fence and US Integrated Fixed Towers.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Phase-II of the Vibrant Villages Programme, due for launch on 20 February 2026:
1. Its launch was planned from Kargil in Ladakh.
2. It builds a separate delivery system instead of relying on convergence of existing schemes.
3. Its four saturation themes are defence roads, bunkers, helipads and fencing.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. The launch was planned from Cachar district in Assam by the Union Home Minister. Delivery relies on convergence of schemes rather than a parallel system. The four themes are civilian: all-weather roads, telecom, television connectivity and electrification. The security logic is indirect, since prosperous, connected villages keep residents in place and make them the 'eyes and ears' of border-guarding forces.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 72

questions.q:
With reference to bodies and tools in India's counter-terrorism framework, consider the following statements:
1. A Combating Financing of Terrorism Cell exists in the Ministry of Home Affairs.
2. The Counter Terrorism and Counter Radicalization Division monitors online radicalisation.
3. The Bureau of Police Research and Development provides specialised tactical training.
4. The Ministry of Home Affairs is India's central authority for mutual legal assistance in criminal matters.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct, showing how finance, online activity, capacity and foreign evidence are divided among bodies. The finance cell dates to 2011, and the Bureau shares tactical training with the NSG. Extradition, by contrast, falls to the Ministry of External Affairs. PRAHAAR treats these treaties, extradition arrangements and Joint Working Groups as tools for sharing evidence and legal cooperation across borders.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80; central authority for MLATs is static

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: INS Anjadip is built to detect, track and neutralise enemy submarines in the littoral environment.
Statement-II: INS Anjadip is the third of eight Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but the second does not explain the first. Its position in a production series and the name of its builder say nothing about why the craft is designed for coastal waters. The role comes from the threat of submarines in shallow seas, which needs indigenous sensors such as the hull-mounted sonar Abhay. That capability earns it the 'Dolphin Hunter' label.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 72

questions.q:
Solar pumps and distribution reform are recommended to fix farm power supply. Consider the following statements:
1. The Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme is a scheme of the Ministry of Power.
2. PM-KUSUM, the main solar pump scheme, is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. RDSS links financial support to reform milestones like smart metering and feeder segregation. Statement 2 is wrong as PM-KUSUM belongs to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, although its beneficiaries are farmers. NITI Aayog recommended solar pumps in 2021 to lower procurement costs and subsidy burdens, which would ease pressure on State distribution companies' finances.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 75-78; ministries for RDSS and PM-KUSUM are static

questions.q:
With reference to the terrain and places mentioned in India's border-management news, consider the following statements:
1. India's longest international land border is with Bangladesh.
2. The marshes of Gujarat form part of the border with Pakistan.
3. Assam's international borders are with Bhutan and Bangladesh.
4. Cachar district lies in Assam's Barak Valley.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. The eastern riverine border with Bangladesh and the Gujarat marshes are the stretches where fencing leaves gaps, which is why technology is favoured there. Assam does not touch Myanmar; the Indian States that do are Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram. Cachar, in the Barak Valley of southern Assam, was named as the launch site for Phase-II of the Vibrant Villages Programme.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 70-71; Vision IAS p. 72; border facts are static

questions.q: 'Hawala', named in India's counter-terror financing work, is best described as:
o: a cryptocurrency mixing service on the dark web
an informal transfer of value through trusted operators, without physical or formal banking movement of money across the route
a licensed cross-border payments system regulated by the Reserve Bank of India
an Islamic bond issued by governments in West Asia
questions.e: In hawala, one broker receives money and a counterpart elsewhere pays out, settling accounts later through trust, so no funds travel through regular channels and few records exist. That makes it attractive for terror financing and explains the MHA cell's focus. It is not a regulated banking system. An Islamic bond is a sukuk, and crypto mixers are a distinct, newer tool in illicit finance.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 68-70; Shankar IAS pp. 78-80; working of hawala is static
